It is thought that capacitation allows the sperm to use a combination of enzymes and neuraminidase to digest down and through the Corona Radiata layer.  The outer layer of the ovum consists of roughly 20-40 squamous epithelial cells, each surrounded by a layer of heavily glycosylated glycoproteins.  Capacitation is thought to also allow the sperm to undergo the acrosome reaction, which is a requirement for penetration of the Zona Pellucida layer of the ovum.  The acrosome reaction allows the release of proteolytic enzymes from the outer acrosomal region of the sperm, which digest a path through the Zona Pellucida.  The Zona Pellucida layer is a thick layer of glycoproteins surrounding the oocyte, which prevents polyspermy (the fertilization of an oocyte by more than one sperm).  Prevention of polyspermy is achieved by two mechanisms:1. Cushing’s disease is a form of hypercortisolemia caused by pituitary-secreted cortisol. Patients with Cushing’s disease have a pituitary tumour secreting excess adrenocorticotrophic hormone (ACTH), which stimulates the adrenal glands to produce excess cortisol. Patients with Cushing’s syndrome, on the other hand, have elevated cortisol levels that are not caused by a pituitary tumour. Patients with Cushing’s syndrome may have adrenal hyperplasia or an adrenal adenoma/carcinoma.  Patients with Cushing’s disease have low cortisol levels on an overnight dexamethasone suppression test (DST). In contrast, patients with Cushing’s syndrome have normal or high DSTs. C: In patients with Cushing’s disease, somatic cells would not respond to cortisol because there is no cortisol being produced. Digoxin increases the strength of contractions of the heart by increasing the amount of calcium ions taken up into the myocytes. It does this by blocking Na+/K+ ATPase in the BL. This traps sodium in the cell which reduces the effectiveness of NCX antiporter. This means more calcium is taken up via the L-type voltage gated calcium channels.

The rotator cuff muscles are the four muscles which hold the head of the humerus in the glenoid cavity during movement of the upper limb. They are: Supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis. Each acts as a muscle of the rotator cuff, but they also have other roles. Supraspinatus: 0-15 degrees abductionInfraspinatus: Lateral rotation of the arm at the GH jointTeres minor: Lateral rotation of the arm at the GH joint and abduction of the trunk. Also helps to stabilise the shoulder.Acts as a muscle to stabilise the glenohumeral joint throughout a wide range of motion. Contained in two subscapular spaces.

Sentinel cells (also known as pathfinder cells) are a group of cells that reside in peripheral tissues ready to detect invasion by pathogens. They include the dendritic cells, macrophages and mast cells. They play a crucial role in innate immunity.  NK cells (natural killer cells) are a type of cytotoxic lymphocyte that forms a key part of the innate immune system. They kill target cells (infected by a virus or tumour) before the adaptive immune system is fully activated.  All the others are cells that would be considered as sentinel cells!  More info here: https://teachmephysiology.com/immune-system/innate-immune-system/sentinel-cells/

D is the correct answer. Clopidogrel is an anti-platelet drug that prevents initiated platelets activating other platelets and starting a chain reaction. Aspirin is an anti-platelet drug that inhibits the production of thromboxane A2 which prevents platelets from activating other platelets and starting a chain reaction. These two drugs are given after a myocardial infarction with ST elevation to reduce the incidence of recurrent thrombotic events.Warfarin is an anticoagulant that inhibits the production of factors II, VII, IX and X. It does this by inhibiting the enzyme involved in the synthesis of a functional form of vit. K. The anticoagulant effect is delayed because anticoagulant effect is consumed from the body's stores of a functional vit K. Rivaroxaban is an anticoagulant that inhibits factor Xa. NOAC = non-vitamin-oral anti-coagulant. Dabigatran is an anticoagulant that inhibits the action of thrombin. Giving these anticoagulants together increases the risk of bleeding so aspirin is often continued in patients on warfarin or a NOAC if they have a history of vascular disease.

HCN4 channels are hyperpolarised cyclic gated inwardly rectifying potassium channels. Activation by noradrenaline causes increased pacemaking activity in SA node - therefore an increase in heart rate (chronotropy) Ryanodine receptors are the receptors activated by high intracellular Ca2+ levels that open to release more Ca2+ from the SR. CICR therefore increases the amount of Ca2+ available for contraction - therefore an increase in Inotropy (contractility).  Lucitropy is the effect on the rate of relaxation of the myocytes.  Answer B is therefore correct while D is incorrect as lucitropy is increased not decreased.

Aldosterone causes sodium retention, which in turn causes water retention. It also causes potassium secretion. ADH stimulation is a secondary effect of aldosterone as increased sodium reabsorption increases osmolarity, which stimulates the release of ADH from the posterior pituitary. Increased ADH release leads to increased water reabsorption by the kidneys.Renin Activating Hormone (renin is released by the juxtaglomerular cells in the kidney in response to decreased blood pressure) up regulates the aldosterone-renin-aldosterone complex.
